description:
Establish transpose and logical-buffer comparison arms. Establish reproducible operation-equivalent external baselines without changing production kernels.

## Background

M4RI matrix operations, Bitshuffle bit-plane transforms and ISA-L parity operations overlap only for explicitly mapped cells. Reuse their relevant capabilities without treating different layouts as interchangeable.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Satisfy the [Zen 3 measurement contract](dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md) for correctness, reproducible release benchmarks, comparison validity and adoption; receipts pin its committed version, the frozen protocol and the cell addendum. Include mandatory before/after evidence for production changes and preserve negative outcomes.

- [hard] REQ-02: Pin M4RI, Bitshuffle and ISA-L revisions, licenses, build flags and selected backend evidence for transpose, logical/parity and consuming matrix cells.

- [hard] REQ-03: Define and validate operation-equivalent bit mappings, matrix/tile dimensions, padding, aliasing and parity arity. Measure Bitshuffle geometry adaptation and ISA-L input/output arrangement; record unavailable comparisons explicitly.

- [hard] REQ-04: Commit frozen family addenda and baseline receipts for canonical 64x64 transpose/conversion cells and logical buffers around 8-64 words, including neighboring sizes, boundaries, alignment and consumer setup/conversion.

- [hard] REQ-05: Reuse established BCH harnesses for contextual conversion cells without waiting for a separate encoder performance campaign. No historical pre-cutover receipt substitutes for a current pinned before measurement.

## Notes

Pin exact source and build identities in the family addendum. Preserve unavailable, incompatible and losing arms rather than substituting a different operation.

Source references: [AlbrechtBard2026], [Bitshuffle2026], [IsaL2026].
title: Establish transpose and logical-buffer comparison arms
